clue.text: A French couple needed to relax

parts.note: un is the French for a
a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Someone needs a pair of French companions in order to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbrace is to loosen tension, so it means to slacken or unwind.

clue.text: Enough to make a hearty editor feel faint?

definitions.text: Enough to make a hearty editor feel faint?

parts.words: Enough to make a hearty editor feel faint?
parts.note: read medically, poor blood flow can cause fainting; read as journalism, a newspaper editor is upset by low sales figures

explanation.definitionFit: Poor blood flow in the body, and for a paper, low numbers of copies sold.

clue.text: A big hit turned back the alliance

indicators.note: the word for the hit is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: in cricket a six is a big hit clearing the boundary

explanation.surface: A heavy blow pushed the coalition into retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned back' makes XIS. A six is a cricket hit over the boundary, worth six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: Stay back with Leslie to have some food

indicators.note: the word for stay is taken back, read in reverse

parts.note: to bide is to stay or wait
Les is the short form of the name Leslie

explanation.surface: Staying behind with Leslie to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to eat, items of foodstuff.

clue.text: Dummies found in ruined sofa

indicators.note: a ruined sofa is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mannequins discovered lying in a wrecked settee.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummies and oafs are both slang for clumsy, stupid people.

clue.text: A person scorned for striking players?

explanation.surface: Someone shunned because actors walked off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is rejected by society; read as two words, it is a troupe of performers who are on strike.

clue.text: Apprehension felt by Egyptian in remote surroundings

indicators.note: the word for remote forms surroundings around the letter for Egyptian

parts.note: far means distant or remote
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: An Egyptian in a distant place feels anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension is anxiety about what may happen, a synonym of dread.

clue.text: Hollow warning from schoolboys after study

indicators.note: after places the schoolboys' warning behind the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
cave, Latin for beware, was public-school slang for 'look out'

explanation.surface: A warning cry from pupils following a session of revision.
explanation.walkthrough: Cave (said KAY-vee) was a lookout's cry at British public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A concave surface curves inward like the inside of a bowl, so it is hollowed.

clue.text: Nether Wallop

parts.note: Nether Wallop is a real Hampshire village; read literally, nether means lower and a wallop is a hard blow, so a blow to the backside

explanation.walkthrough: Nether Wallop is a village in Hampshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot to the backside, or figuratively a sharp spur to action.

clue.text: Government with main traditions for reform

indicators.note: the letters are put up for reform, that is reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A new government promises to reform the country's main traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: The administration is the executive that runs a country, a synonym for the government of the day.

clue.text: He brings a duck back fresh

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

indicators.note: the word for fresh is brought back, read in reverse

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: A man brings home a duck that is newly caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so a male person, 'he'.

clue.text: Stray cardinal has a condition?

parts.note: W, west, is one of the cardinal points of the compass
if introduces a condition, as in 'if it rains'

explanation.surface: A churchman of high rank appears to suffer from an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prince of the Church, but here it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless, stray child or animal.

clue.text: Quietly start to pray

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
to lead is to start off or go first

explanation.surface: Someone begins a quiet prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to beg earnestly, a synonym for pray in the sense of entreat.

clue.text: Ladies' fingers depicted by acceptable artist

parts.note: OK means all right, acceptable
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A competent painter has portrayed a woman's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies' fingers is the British name for the green pod vegetable, not a woman's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender green seed pods of the plant are known in Britain by that name, after their shape.

clue.text: Nothing follows fast for it is very slow

indicators.note: follows places the zero after the period of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Fasting brings nothing, since it is a very slow process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like 'quick', the opposite of the definition, but it is the fasting season.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning a slow pace.

clue.text: In time a theologian may be addressed as father

indicators.note: In puts the theologian's letters inside the word for time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree

explanation.surface: In time, a scholar of religion may be called Father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a priest's title, fitting the theologian, but it is a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a child's informal word for a male parent.

clue.text: The heart of the matter

parts.note: read as physics: matter is made of atoms, and each atom has a dense central core

explanation.definitionFit: The core of an atom, the central part of matter, and figuratively the central point of anything.

clue.text: Aintree disaster for apprentice

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National

explanation.surface: A racing calamity at Aintree for a novice jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the English racecourse of the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is someone learning a trade, a learner or novice.

clue.text: Tested the sharpness of sword and pen

parts.note: felt means touched to test, as with a finger
the sharp point of a blade is its tip

explanation.surface: Someone checked the edge of a blade and of a writing instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'the pen is mightier than the sword'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a porous fibre writing point is named for that nib.

clue.text: Place for shooting stars?

parts.note: read as cinema rather than astronomy: where famous actors are filmed

explanation.definitionFit: The stage or location where a movie is shot, with actors as the celebrities.

clue.text: Give a graphic description of the harbour light

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Describe vividly the beam shining at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent vividly, in words or pictures.

clue.text: Critical comment-from a theatre critic?

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark made by a reviewer of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation it is British disapproval ('poor effort!'), and literally it is a poor performance a reviewer might pan.

clue.text: Aggregate and aluminium found in dynamite

indicators.note: found in puts the metal's symbol inside the word for an explosion

parts.note: a blast is an explosion, what dynamite produces
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Crushed stone and a metal discovered in explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggregate' is a noun: crushed stone or gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is gravel or crushed stone used as a bed for railway tracks, a kind of construction aggregate.

clue.text: Plant of very little note

parts.note: wee is Scots for small or very little
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A plant of hardly any importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of very little note' reads as 'unimportant'; split it, it gives a tiny word plus a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is an unwanted wild plant.

clue.text: Many didn't drink after time

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword 'many'
someone who ate took food rather than drink

explanation.surface: Lots of people abstained from alcohol after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late comes behind schedule, past the expected hour.

clue.text: Note the record is amusing

parts.note: D is a musical note
a roll is an official register or record, as in electoral roll

explanation.surface: Observe that the gramophone disc is funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means humorous in a dry or quaint way.

clue.text: Mushy peas divine to a Scot

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed, so the letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish fondness for mushy peas, a British side dish of mashed peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective (heavenly) praising the peas; it is the verb meaning to foretell. Mushy peas are a British chip-shop side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Spae is a Scots verb meaning to foretell or prophesy.

clue.text: Related some stories in a kindly way

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words a kindly

explanation.surface: Told a few tales in a gentle manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Related' looks like the verb 'told', which suits the stories; it is the adjective meaning of the same family.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means of similar kind or kin, a synonym of related.

clue.text: See about a thousand duck

indicators.note: the word See goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Look at roughly a thousand waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Smee is an old name for a duck, the wigeon or the smew.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect name for certain wild ducks such as the smew or pintail.

clue.text: Hairdressing provided in casualty department

explanation.surface: A hair salon service on offer at the hospital emergency unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, it is care given to a shaggy mass of hair; medically, it is electric or emergency therapy for a patient in trauma.

clue.text: I meet North Kentucky black

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: I am meeting a man from northern Kentucky in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inky is as dark as ink.

clue.text: Time to think logically about a disloyal act

parts.note: to reason is to think things through logically

explanation.surface: Time to weigh up an act of betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or ruler.
